Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

gently adverb

also softly, gentle (be gentle), be gentle!, easy does it, lightly, tenderly

classical

Cic. Rep. 6.12: lēniter arrīdēns (Lewis & Short)
Ov. Am. 1.6.7: lēniter īre per excubiās custōdum (Lewis & Short)
Cato Agr. 75

lēniter

adverb · Wiktionary

gently, softly, mildly

Of movement, speech and heat alike; of a slope, gradually (collis lēniter acclīvis, Caes. B.G. 7.19).

Other words

  • molliter — softly, gently, tenderly

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Ps. 5.2.7: molliter sustinē mē (Lewis & Short); Cic. N.D. 2.129: avēs nīdōs mollissimē substernunt (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    Of touch and handling: softly, so as not to hurt or break.

  • placidē — calmly, quietly, without hurry

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 4.7.35: forem aperīre (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Ps. 242; Ter. Ph. 5.6.27: īre (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    Said on its own to someone rushing: placidē!, gently, easy now.

Examples

  • Quid properās? placidē.

    What’s the hurry? Gently.Plaut. Ps. 242

  • in focō caldō sub testū coquitō lēniter

    bake it gently on a hot hearth under a crockCato Agr. 75

  • quasi admīrāns stetit ac deinde sēnsim atque placidē, tamquam nōscitābundus, ad hominem accēdit

    he stopped as if amazed, and then slowly and gently, as though recognising him, came up to the manGell. 5.14.11

  • Molliter tractā fēlem.

    Be gentle with the cat.composed

See also gentle, soft, carefully.
